plugins.name: cstack
plugins.description: Crishon's own Claude Code skills (deslop, write-a-skill, bootstrap-agents, upkeep) and the claims-auditor agent, which checks finished work against what was claimed. Borrowed skills are pinned pointers listed below, not copies.

plugins.name: plain
plugins.description: Keeps everything we publish readable for a junior developer or product manager with no outside context: writing rules, a checker, a blank cold reader, plain-English dark diagrams with a contrast checker, and a hold before posting. Opt in per repository with .claude/plain.json.

plugins.name: verify
plugins.description: Proves that work works, not only that tests pass: a proof standard, a check that specs and plans name their evidence, one verification skill per app (created by verify-setup, kept honest by verify-upkeep), shared guides for driving web and Expo apps, and the pr-review skill: claims auditor plus Codex verdicts tied to the commit, posted as one plain-English comment.

plugins.name: agent-browser
plugins.description: Pinned external: vercel-labs browser-automation skill (was 'dogfood' in Hermes skills-lock)

plugins.name: pstack-picks
plugins.description: Pinned pointer to Lauren Tan's pstack skills (pstack 0.15.13, MIT). Coding: TypeScript best practices and her engineering principles (simplicity, types, boundaries, testing behavior, root causes). Review and design: architect, blast radius, correct, interrogate, how, why, no comments. Building the system itself: swarm, arena, reflect, figure it out, benchmark checklist, recall, show your work, never block on the human, encode lessons in structure. Also unslop and her two verification tools. Most principles are invoked by name, not loaded automatically.

plugins.name: ponytail-picks
plugins.description: Pinned pointer to Ponytail (Dietrich Gebert, MIT): the simplest change that fully solves the task. You aren't going to need it, use what already exists, standard library first, delete before adding. Six skills: ponytail, review, audit, debt, gain, help. Only the skills are picked, so its always-on hooks are not installed; call it when wanted.

plugins.name: rn-callstack-picks
plugins.description: Pinned pointer to three of Callstack's React Native skills (MIT): performance (frames per second, bundle size, startup time, native), React Navigation, and React Native upgrades. Install only in projects with a React Native app.

plugins.name: rn-vercel-picks
plugins.description: Pinned pointer to Vercel's React Native coding rules (lists, animation, navigation, UI patterns, state, monorepos). Pointer only: the source repository has no license file. Install only in projects with a React Native app.

plugins.name: expo-picks
plugins.description: Pinned pointer to Expo's own skills (Expo, MIT): the router, native UI, data fetching, animation, modules, app store builds, over-the-air updates, workflows and upgrades. Install only in projects with an Expo app.

plugins.name: vercel-react-picks
plugins.description: Pinned pointer to Vercel's React and web interface skills: React performance rules, component composition patterns, view transitions, and the web interface guidelines review. Pointer only: the repository has no license file, though its readme says MIT. Install only in projects with a React web app.

plugins.name: vercel-deploy-picks
plugins.description: Pinned pointer to Vercel's deploy skills: deploying to Vercel, using its command line with tokens, and making a deployed app faster and cheaper. Pointer only, for the same license reason. Install only in projects hosted on Vercel.

plugins.name: good-css-picks
plugins.description: Pinned pointer to good-css (Vojta Holik and contributors, MIT): 47 modern CSS techniques borrowed from CSS experts, written for agents. Read its skill before writing or reviewing any web styles (plain CSS, Tailwind, CSS-in-JS); it names which reference file to read for each task. Web only: it doesn't apply to React Native styles.

plugins.name: caveman-picks
plugins.description: Pinned pointer to caveman (Julius Brussee, Apache 2.0): a terse reply mode that cuts tokens while keeping every technical fact, with its two stronger modes (ultra and wenyan). cstack used to carry an older copy of it.
